findings.title: Login cache invalidation on update fails when an organization is disabled or when a cached IDP is mutated in-place
findings.body: In `update(IdentityProviderModel model)`, `idpById = getById(model.getInternalId())` returns a model wrapped by `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel`, where `isEnabled()` returns `false` whenever the linked organization is disabled, even if the IDP itself is enabled in storage. Meanwhile, `getForLogin` populates its cache from `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...)`, which includes enabled IDPs belonging to disabled organizations. Because `LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` checks `IdentityProviderModel::isEnabled`, when an organization is disabled `getLoginPredicate().test(original)` is always `false`. If an IDP in that disabled organization (whose `internalId` is cached in `getForLogin`) is updated to be unavailable for login (e.g., `hideOnLogin = true`, `linkOnly = true`, or `BROKER_PUBLIC = false`), `getLoginPredicate().test(updated)` is also `false`, so `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate` returns early without invalidating `cacheKeyForLogin`; once the organization is re-enabled, the hidden/link-only/private IDP will still be returned by `getForLogin`. Conversely, if `updated` was also obtained via `getById`/`getByAlias` (so it is also wrapped) and updated to become login-eligible while the organization is disabled, both predicates evaluate to `false` and the cache is again not invalidated. Furthermore, when `Profile.Feature.ORGANIZATION` is disabled, `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel` returns the cached `IdentityProviderModel` reference without copying it, so mutating a model from `getById` in-place and passing it to `update(model)` causes `original` and `updated` to be the same instance and skips invalidation.

findings.title: `remove(String alias)` leaves stale `internalId` entries in cache when IDP was only cached via `getById`
findings.body: In `remove(String alias)`, `getForLogin` (line 246) and `getByOrganization` (line 202) populate the cache by calling `session.identityProviders().getById(id)`, which caches `CachedIdentityProvider` under `internalId` without populating `cacheKeyIdpAlias(realm, alias)`. When `remove(alias)` is later called for such an IDP, `isInvalid(cacheKey)` is `false` and `realmCache.getCache().get(cacheKey, CachedIdentityProvider.class)` returns `null`, so `registerIDPInvalidation` is never called despite `storedIdp` already having been loaded on line 100. As a result, the `internalId` cache entry remains in `realmCache`, causing subsequent `getById` and `getByOrganization` calls to return the deleted IDP. Additionally, if `remove(alias)` is called with a non-existent alias while `isInvalid(cacheKey)` is `true`, `registerIDPInvalidation(storedIdp)` on line 103 will throw a `NullPointerException` because `storedIdp` is `null`.

findings.title: `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin` returns disabled IDPs when their organization is disabled
findings.body: The contract of `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin` specifies that only enabled identity providers suitable for login are returned. `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin` wraps returned models with `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel` (which makes `idp.isEnabled()` return `false` when the linked organization is disabled), but does not filter the resulting stream by `IdentityProviderModel::isEnabled`. Instead, the `idp.isEnabled()` filter was added only in `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean`, leaving `getForLogin` itself returning disabled IDPs to any other caller.

findings.title: Test cleanup in `testCacheIDPForLogin` uses literal `"alias"` instead of the created IDP alias
findings.body: Lines 381 and 425 register cleanup callbacks using `testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove` with the hardcoded string `"alias"` instead of `idpRep.getAlias()` (`"idp-alias-" + i` and `"idp-alias-20"`). Because no IDP with alias `"alias"` exists, the cleanup calls fail with HTTP 404 (ignored by `TestCleanup`) and the realm-level IDPs created by `testCacheIDPForLogin` are never removed from the test realm.
